name: Romanian folk sky
summary: 39 figures of the Romanian peasant tradition: farm tools, pastoral life and Christian images in the sky.

UMa.name: Great Cart
UMa.description: The stars of the Great Bear, which in Romanian tradition form a great cart. It corresponds to the Hungarian Wain of Göncöl, but here the cart also includes further stars of the Great Bear.

C3i.name: Goat with Three Kids
C3i.description: In the constellation Auriga: the bright Capella is the mother goat, and the three fainter stars next to it are her kids. Hungarian tradition also calls Capella the Goat Kid.

Csa.name: Scythe
Csa.description: A scythe drawn from the stars of Cepheus. Romanian folk tradition also saw the sky as an “exhibition” of peasant tools.

Cio.name: Shepherd with His Sheep
Cio.description: In the constellation Lyra: the bright Vega is the shepherd, and the fainter stars around it are his sheep.

Hra.name: Round Dance
Hra.description: The semicircle of stars of Corona Borealis are the dancers of a hora, a round dance.

Jgb.name: Well and Trough
Jgb.description: The great square of Pegasus and the row of stars of Andromeda together form a well and its trough.

Tdz.name: God’s Throne
Tdz.description: The W-shaped row of stars of Cassiopeia, in which tradition saw the throne of God. In Hungarian tradition the same figure is the Holy Well.

Fap.name: Emperor’s Daughter with the Water Yoke
Fap.description: In the constellation Aquila: the bright Altair is the emperor’s daughter, and the two neighbouring stars (Tarazed and Alshain) are the two buckets of the water yoke she carries on her shoulder.

Ccp.name: Hen with Her Chicks
Ccp.description: The Pleiades are, in Romanian tradition too, a hen with her chicks, just as in Hungarian.

UMi.name: Little Cart
UMi.description: The stars of the Little Bear, the smaller counterpart of the Great Cart; the Pole Star is at the end of its shaft.

Gem.name: The Brothers
Gem.description: The two bright stars of Gemini (Castor and Pollux) and the rows of stars belonging to them: two brothers.

Pma.name: Great Cross
Pma.description: The great cross of the constellation Cygnus in the summer Milky Way. Hungarian tradition also calls it the Cross.

Pmi.name: Little Cross
Pmi.description: The tiny rhombus-shaped group of stars of Delphinus. In Hungarian tradition the same figure is the Little Cross.

Cap.name: The Billy Goat
Cap.description: The stars of Capricornus, a billy goat in Romanian tradition.

Rac.name: The River Crab
Rac.description: The faint stars of the constellation Cancer.

Cal.name: The Horse
Cal.description: In the constellation Leo, Romanian tradition saw a horse; the sickle-shaped head and the body follow the stars of the western Lion.

Dra.name: The Dragon
Dra.description: The long winding row of stars of Draco, the dragon (balaur) of Romanian folk tales.

Crb.name: The Raven
Crb.description: A figure made of the four bright stars of the constellation Corvus.

Cat.name: The Scales
Cat.description: The stars of Libra, a hand-held steelyard (cântar) in Romanian tradition.

Vir.name: The Maiden
Vir.description: The stars of Virgo, with the bright Spica.

Psc.name: The Carps
Psc.description: The two strings of fish of Pisces, carps in Romanian tradition.

Ber.name: The Ram
Ber.description: The stars of the constellation Aries.

Cma.name: The Hound
Cma.description: The constellation Canis Major, with Sirius in it: in Romanian tradition a large guard dog (dulău).

Ctl.name: The Puppy
Ctl.description: The two stars of Canis Minor, the bright Procyon and Gomeisa.

Vca.name: The Cowherd
Vca.description: The constellation Boötes, in Romanian tradition a cowherd grazing the cows. The folk name of the bright Arcturus in Hungarian (Ökörhajcsár, the Oxherd) is also linked to a herdsman.

Prb.name: The Little Dove
Prb.description: The stars of the constellation Columba.

Var.name: The One Who Pours Out Water
Var.description: The stars of Aquarius: a figure pouring water from a jug.

Chi.name: The Whale
Chi.description: The stars of the constellation Cetus.

Rar.name: The Little Plough
Rar.description: A small plough (rariță) drawn from the stars of Orion (the shoulders, the belt and the legs). Romanian folk tradition also saw the sky as an “exhibition” of peasant tools. Four Romanian figures overlap in Orion.

Sec.name: The Sickle
Sec.description: A sickle drawn from the fainter stars around Orion’s Sword. Romanian folk tradition also saw the sky as an “exhibition” of peasant tools.

Sfm.name: The Great Auger
Sfm.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt and Rigel: a large carpenter’s auger. Romanian folk tradition also saw the sky as an “exhibition” of peasant tools.

Tau.name: The Bull
Tau.description: The V-shaped Hyades that form the head of Taurus, and the reddish Aldebaran.

Omu.name: The Man
Omu.description: The stars of Hercules, simply a human figure in Romanian tradition.

Sar.name: The Serpent
Sar.description: The stars of Ophiuchus and Serpens together form a single great serpent.

Sco.name: The Scorpion
Sco.description: The stars of Scorpius with the reddish Antares.

Bar.name: The Broadaxe
Bar.description: A broad axe (barda) drawn from the stars of Perseus. Romanian folk tradition also saw the sky as an “exhibition” of peasant tools.

Arc.name: The Archer
Arc.description: The bright stars of Sagittarius: an archer.

Trf.name: The Three Saints
Trf.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt, in Romanian tradition the three holy church fathers whose common feast day is on 30 January. In Hungarian tradition the same figure is the Reapers’ Star.

Vri.name: The Wild Boars
Vri.description: The stars of the Hyades and Aldebaran, the same as in The Bull figure: another tradition saw wild boars in them.
